title: Fractional SLI and Panel Decking for Multi-tenant Dashboards
content:
Purpose:
This note collects an experiment-forward approach to defining fractional SLIs (SLI that represent weighted proportions rather than binary pass/fail), and how to "deck" (tile) compact dashboard panels for multi-tenant surfaces so operators can triage quickly under query-cost constraints. Meant as a working sketch for the observability sprint (Q1 2026).

Why fractional SLIs?
- Classic binary SLI (request meets 200ms P99) is easy but brittle for multi-tenant inference where tenant sizes vary by 1000x.
- Fractional SLI lets us express the "share" of traffic that meets a target at different percentiles and weight by tenant importance.
- This supports fairness (avoid a few noisy tenants dominating the global SLI) and provides more actionable signals for mitigation (e.g., isolate top-K offenders).

Core definitions (working):
- request: a single API call as seen by the gateway (includes multi-turn chat requests counted as 1 request).
- token-latency: time from first token request to last token emitted (ms).
- qP(x): the xth percentile of token-latency across requests in a window. e.g., qP(95) = 95th percentile.
- fractional_sli_V(T, p, w): for tenant T, percentile p, and weight w (0..1), the contribution is w * indicator(qP_T(p) <= target_p). Global fractional SLI = sum_T fractional_sli_V(T,p,w) / sum_T w.
- example weight schemes: equal-weight-per-tenant, volume-weight (requests per minute), revenue-weight.

Metric primitives to record (instrumentation notes):
- per-request: request_id, tenant_id (hashed), route, model_version, request_start, response_end, token_count, cold_cache_flag (bool), kv_hit_rate (float 0..1).
- per-aggregation window (1m, 5m): p50/p95/p99 token-latency per tenant, request_count_per_tenant, cold_cache_percent.
- derived: tenant-weighted-availability (fractional SLI), tenant-longevity (90-day request share), and cold-warm split panels.

Trace sampling strategy (cheap but informative):
- Goals: keep trace cost manageable; ensure high-fidelity traces for outliers and for each tenant top-N contributors to variance.
- Two-stage sampler idea (to prototype):
  1) Lightweight probe in the ingest path computes anomaly_score = normalized(token-latency / expected_latency_by-route) * (1 + cold_cache_flag).
  2) Deterministic keep probability = min(0.0005 + anomaly_score * 0.02, 0.5) capped per-tenant to avoid over-sampling one customer.
  3) Always keep N per-minute for each tenant (N=2 default) for baseline.
- Implementation notes: rely on the runtime fast-path (no blocking) to emit a sampling hint to the trace service; sampling decisions should be idempotent for retries.

Dashboard decking (compact multi-tenant layout):
- Constraints: limited vertical real-estate on mobile and thin-client UIs; query cost budget (production dashboard queries must be < X tokens per day).
- Decking proposal (left-to-right, top-to-bottom):
  Row A (operator quick-scan): global fractional SLI (single sparkline with stacked tenant contributions), global request-rate, global error-rate.
  Row B (variance lens): heatmap (tenant vs percentile) with toggle: show top-50 tenants by request volume or by variance. Hover shows tenant id, recent change, and quick-links to traces.
  Row C (cost and warmness): per-tenant KV-warmth bar, per-tenant median token count, estimated cost per-tenant (rolling 24h).
  Row D (investigation): top 5 sampled traces summary (latency waterfall text), last successful canary results, rollout gate indicator for active rollouts.
- Compact widget behaviors: sparklines should default to 1h but support quick expand; heatmaps must use server-side quantization to keep queries cheap.

Alerting and SLO mapping (how fractional SLI ties to alerts):
- Global fractional SLI < 0.95 (for revenue-weight) triggers P2 ops alert.
- Tenant-level fractional SLI drop of >20% over baseline triggers auto-created investigation card (not a noisy Pager).
- Auto-escalation rules: persistent tenant SLI failures for >30m escalate to oncall.

Rollout and validation checklist (for next sprint):
- [ ] implement per-request lightweight fields in gateway log. (owner: Diego)
- [ ] storage: create 5m aggregation table keyed by tenant_id, route, model_version. (owner: Priya)
- [ ] sampling hook: prototype two-stage sampler in runtime canary. (owner: Liam)
- [ ] dashboard seed: craft the decking layout in Grafana sandbox with synthetic data. (owner: Maya)
- [ ] alert rules: author fractional SLI alerting playbook and do noise tests. (owner: Maya + SRE rotation)
- [ ] run a 2-week shadow run comparing equal-weight vs revenue-weight fractional SLI.

Open questions / discussion topics (for 1:1 and working session):
- What is the canonical tenant weight? Revenue-weight is business-meaningful but leaks pricing information in dashboards—should we map revenue to obfuscated tiers?
- How to represent multi-model fanout requests (one API call fans out to 3 models) in SLI accounting? Attribute to origin request, or split by model?
- Sampling fairness: enforce a hard cap per customer per-hour, but how to handle customers with legitimately bursty test traffic?

Notes to self / short-term heuristics:
- Start with revenue-weight obfuscated to bands (bronze/silver/gold) to avoid precise dollar exposure.
- Use 5-minute aggregation windows for alerting thresholds, 1-minute for hot investigation dashboards.
- For early prototyping keep sampling bias low (base 0.05%) and tweak after we have anomaly distributions.

References and links:
- see linked artifacts at top for current PR + tickets.
- related idea: "partitioned SLI" sketch in CONFLUENCE-OBS-6204 (we should unify vocabulary).

Appendix: quick formula cheat-sheet
- tenant_qP(p, w): compute qP for tenant over window W.
- fractional_sli_global(p) = sum_T w_T * I(tenant_qP_T(p) <= target_p) / sum_T w_T.
- anomaly_score ~ (latency / expected_by_route) + cold_cache_flag * 0.5 + (token_count > route_median_token * 3 ? 0.2 : 0).

Quick wins (2-day experiments):
- instrument cold_cache_flag and re-run heatmap decking with that column visible.
- add per-tenant N=2 trace keep rule and confirm storage/ingest costs.

If helpful I can convert this into a short slide deck for the weekly observability sync.
